newsitem.title: DENMARK: SOCCER-DENMARK WIN ENDS 30-MATCH UNBEATEN RUN FOR FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DENMARK WIN ENDS 30-MATCH UNBEATEN RUN FOR FRANCE.

text.p: A single goal by Per Pedersen was sufficient to end France's three-year, 30-match unbeaten run when Denmark beat them 1-0 in a friendly international on Saturday.
The young striker halted the French run with one moment of panache in an otherwise dull match.
Closely marked by France's Marcel Desailly, Pedersen had his back to the goal when he received the ball from Marc Rieper but deftly used an overhead scissors kick to blast the ball in the net.
It was Pedersen's first goal in a full international and it was also France's first defeat since they lost to Bulgaria in November 1993.
France, hosts for next year's World Cup, struggled to equalise but their best attempts, by Zinedine Zidane and Patrice Loko, failed to beat Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel.
The delight of the Danish fans was matched only by French coach Aime Jacquet's disgust with his side's performance.
"Nothing happend, it was a totally negative game, with a concentration of the worst play I have ever seen since I became a selector," he said.
